_doc: The 1904 district's street furniture (T-3199): the gas lamps, (T-3201) the fire hydrants and (T-3202) the poles and wires. GENERATED by tools/lay_prairie_1904_street_furniture.py from data/street_grid/1904.json, data/street_section/1904.json and data/street_trees/1904.json -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. Local ENU metres of data/datum.json; heading_deg is the compass bearing of the street line the item stands along. Drawn by renderers/web/js/street-furniture.js. docs/RESEARCH/prairie_1904_street_furniture.md is the reading; docs/LIBERTIES.md L-prairie-street-lamps-3199, L-prairie-hydrants-3201 and L-prairie-utility-poles-3202 the inventions. `wires` join poles by id; the renderer hangs them from the poles' pins.

gas_lamp.name: gas street lamp
gas_lamp.form: A cast-iron post: a plain round foot on a plinth, a moulded collar, a leafed boss at knee height, a slender shaft, a bell capital under a knobbed ladder bar, four scrolled arms carrying a clear four-sided lantern that tapers out to a projecting rim, a steep four-sided roof, a vent cap and a knob; painted iron. About 3.1 m. Corner lamps stand on a stone footing.
gas_lamp.form_note: Read off the 1811 photograph, Taylor's no. 2135 and the second 2140 photograph, the three that show a post whole and near; its parts and heights from the 1811 print, the clearest (T-3219). Every lamp is drawn with that one post. 1904 is gas: electric standards appear only in pictures dated after it. The scene is a July morning with no night, so no lamp is lit.
gas_lamp.rule_note: The pictures show such lamps at the district's corners and along its parkways

fire_hydrant.name: fire hydrant
fire_hydrant.form: A post fire hydrant: a cast-iron barrel about 0.85 m tall on a flared foot, a band under a domed bonnet with an operating nut on top, and two side nozzles with caps; painted iron.
fire_hydrant.form_note: Read off the owner's crop of the Detroit Publishing Pullman view, the museum's halftone of the same corner and the second 2140 photograph, which show one type. The prints are monochrome; the Detroit view prints the hydrant lighter than the lamp posts, so it is drawn a mid grey, and its colour is reconstructed.
fire_hydrant.rule_note: The pictures show post hydrants on the parkway at Pullman's corner and at 22nd Street; the city's hydrants stood at its corners and along its long blocks

utility_pole.name: utility pole
utility_pole.form: A wooden pole, 9 to 11 m, tapering from its butt; a line pole carries a crossarm with pins and glass insulators, a trolley-wire pole carries the span wire over the street.
utility_pole.form_note: Glessner's pole in the c. 1887 photograph is a plain wooden pole with one crossarm of about six pins; every line pole is drawn after it. The trolley poles' form is not pictured: drawn as plain wooden poles.
utility_pole.what: A wooden pole carrying overhead wires

what_by_class.trolley: A pole holding the span wire of the street railway's overhead

utility_pole.rule_note: Glessner's pole is pictured on 18th Street; the lines down the alleys are drawn by rule

rule_note_by_class.street: The photograph of Glessner's stable shows the line's pole at the alley
rule_note_by_class.trolley: A photograph at 22nd and Prairie shows rails and trolley wires in 22nd Street; the poles that carried them are not pictured

gas_lamp.note: A lamp at every intersection corner of the district's drawn streets, in the corner square 1.5 ft inside both curbs (the curb-return corner, between where the two crossings land), on a stone footing; the pictured mid-block lamps at their lots; the rest of every face at about 160 ft, the two sides of a street staggered, on the parkway 0.4 m off the walk, each moved along the parkway clear of an elm, a carriage walk or an alley mouth. A corner where a face meets a curved return (Calumet at 18th) has no corner of its own.

fire_hydrant.note: The two pictured hydrants where their pictures put them (Pullman's on the Prairie Avenue parkway beside the walk north of 18th Street, Tucker's near the curb toward 22nd Street); then one at every other intersection, at its corners taken in turn, on the avenue's parkway 3.5 m from the corner and 0.45 m inside the curb; and one mid-block on one side of every block face 150 m long or more. Each stands in the grass, clear of the walks, the corner crossings, the carriage walks, the lamps and the elms.

clearance.note: No pole, crossarm or wire touches a 1904 structure (T-3225): tested on the baked models and the context city's blocks as a plan raster of their heights, a pole's face 0.15 m off any wall, fence or roof edge, a crossarm 0.3 m over the roof beneath it, every wire 0.3 m over whatever it crosses as it sags. An alley pole the rule puts into a coach house slides along the alley, then stands further into it, then crosses to its west side; a span through a building steps its poles further in, or is not hung. `moved` lists the poles off the rule's spot, `spans_not_hung` the spans left out.

utility_pole.note: Glessner's pole where the photograph shows it, on 18th Street's south parkway at the stable's corner by the alley; the line on west from it to Indiana Avenue at about 34 m (Taylor 2135 and the Detroit view show no pole on 18th Street east of the alley); a line down every alley on its east side, its end poles 2.5 m in from the mouths and spanned across the cross streets where alleys meet; none on the Prairie Avenue parkways. Each pole clear of the elms, lamps, hydrants, carriage walks and alley mouths, and every pole, crossarm and wire clear of the buildings, coach houses and fences.

note_by_class.trolley: 22nd Street's overhead: a pair of plain poles at about 34 m, one in the north parkway by the curb and one opposite it across the street, a span wire between them at 6.6 m and two contact wires along the street over the tracks at 5.6 m.

Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1811 S. Prairie.

chicagology_1905_field_photo.citation: [1905 S. Prairie Ave. (Marshall Field residence).] Photograph of the house from the west side of the avenue; unknown photographer, undated (file '923prairiefieldhome', the pre-1880 number). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1905 S. Prairie.
chicagology_1905_field_photo.date: undated (file name uses the pre-1880 number)

chicagology_2120_gorton_photo.citation: [2120 S. Prairie Ave. (Clapp / Gorton house).] Photograph of the house from Prairie Avenue south-east of it; unknown photographer, undated (c. 1880s-1900s). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2120 S. Prairie.

chicagology_2140_photo_a.citation: [2140 S. Prairie Ave. (Tucker / Smith house).] Photograph from the south-east corner of Prairie Avenue and 22nd Street, looking north-west across the crossing; unknown photographer, undated (after 1890). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2140 S. Prairie (file '2140prairie1880').
chicagology_2140_photo_a.date: undated (after 1890: the 1890 house at 2130 stands at right)

chicagology_2140_photo_b.citation: [2140 S. Prairie Ave. (Tucker / Smith house).] Photograph of the house from the Prairie Avenue roadway south-east of it; unknown photographer, undated (after 1890). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2140 S. Prairie (second photograph).

cornell_adw_glessner_stable_1887.citation: Unknown photographer, Detail, Glessner House, ca. 1887. ghm_blog_1721_dexter_c1888.citation: George Glessner, [Wirt Dexter house, 1721 S. Prairie Avenue, before the front addition], c. 1888. Photograph in the Glessner House Museum's George Glessner photographs, reproduced on its blog, 'The Early History of Prairie Avenue - Part IV' (2020-07-07).

ghm_blog_pullman_completed.citation: [George M. Pullman residence, 1729 S. Prairie Avenue, completed.] Halftone of a photograph of the finished house from the south-west, across the crossing of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street; unknown photographer, undated (after the 1892 additions). Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'Prairie Avenue in 1874' (blog, 2014-06-16).

ghm_ward_1887_prairie_north_from_20th.citation: 'Prairie Avenue.' Wood engraving in Souvenir of Chicago (Columbus, Ohio: Ward Bros., 1887), the avenue looking north from 20th Street; Glessner House Museum collection ('Prairie Avenue 1887').

glessner_blog_1708_1706_1700_christmas_p.citation: [1708, 1706 and 1700 S. Prairie Avenue, the homes of James and Narcissa Thorne, George and Alice Glessner, and Blewett and Frances Lee.] Photograph from the east side of Prairie Avenue, captioned 'Three of the trees from The Rocks were delivered to these Prairie Avenue homes: (L-R) James and Narcissa Thorne (1708), George and Alice Glessner (1706), and Blewett and Frances Lee (1700)'; photographer not named. Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'The Glessner House Christmas Tree', The Story of a House (blog), 14 December 2021.
glessner_blog_1708_1706_1700_christmas_p.date: undated (after 1902; the blog's context is Christmas 1911)

nypl_dennis_tucker_1010_prairie_stereo.citation: P. B. Greene, 'Residence of William F. Tucker. 1010 Prairie Avenue, Chicago.' Stereograph, c. 1876-1881. New York Public Library, Robert N. Dennis collection of stereoscopic views, MFY Dennis Coll 90-F175 (digital ID G90F175_004F).

items.note: Pullman's: the Detroit Publishing view and the Glessner House Museum's halftone of the finished house show a post hydrant on the Prairie Avenue parkway beside the walk, a few metres north of the corner lamp at 18th Street. Read off the owner's crop of the Detroit view: a barrel on a flared foot, a band under a domed bonnet with an operating nut, side nozzle caps. Not a hitching post: none is shown at Pullman's.
Tucker's: the second 2140 photograph has a post hydrant of the same type in its left foreground, on the Prairie Avenue parkway toward 22nd Street.
The Pullman corner: the Detroit Publishing view (1890s) and the Glessner House Museum's halftone of the finished house show the post in a curbed grass plot at the curb corner.
The Glessner corner: J. W. Taylor's photograph no. 2135 (c. 1887-89) shows the post on a small stone footing at the curb corner, between the two crossing ramps.
The Ward Bros. engraving of 1887, looking north from 20th Street, draws a lamp post at the east parkway's corner.
The Tucker corner: P. B. Greene's stereograph (c. 1876-81) shows the post in a curbed grass plot at the curb corner; later photographs of the house show the same kind of lamp on its parkway.
The Glessner townhouses photograph shows a street lamp in front of 1708, at the left of the row.
The 1811 photograph shows the lamp on the parkway beside the walk at the house's north lot line (the same lamp stands at the right edge of the early photograph of 1801).
The 1816 photograph, taken from the walk south-east of the house, shows the lamp beyond the house's south flank, at its south lot line.
The Field house photograph shows the lamp on the parkway beside the walk, before the house's north part.
The 2120 photograph shows the lamp on the parkway beside the walk, just south of the stoop.
The second 2140 photograph shows the lamp on the parkway beside the walk at the Prairie Avenue porch.
George Glessner's photograph of 1721 (c. 1888), taken from the west walk opposite it, has the lamp in its right foreground, a little south of the camera.
